title: Contract Oracle and Synthetic Harness Specification
author: Priya Ramanathan
content:
Summary
-------
This document specifies the Contract Oracle and Synthetic Harness (COSH) used to validate API and runtime behavior across model rollouts, runtime kernel changes, and client SDK updates. COSH is a lightweight, opinionated test harness that generates deterministic synthetic traffic, exercises contract boundaries, and evaluates observable side effects (metrics, traces, logs) against a versioned oracle.

Scope
-----
- Applies to public API surface area used by customer-facing SDKs (text-generation, chat, embeddings, streaming).
- Includes REST and streaming endpoints, request/response schemas, error and retry semantics, and runtime degradation/fallback behavior.
- Excludes internal infra-only endpoints (admin, billing).

Motivation
----------
We run frequent changes to model variants, quantized kernels, and routing policies. Traditional schema-only contract tests miss behavioral regressions introduced by runtime fallback, early-exit streaming, and probabilistic model outputs. COSH provides:
- An executable oracle that encodes expected behaviour for a set of representative prompts and request patterns.
- Synthetic traffic with controlled randomness and determinism seeds so results are reproducible across CI runs.
- Observability assertions that verify telemetry emission and stability during rollouts.

Definitions
-----------
- Oracle: A versioned artifact (JSON) that contains canonical expectations for a request set: normalized tokens, expected status classes, allowed ranges for numeric scores, and required telemetry labels.
- Harness: The executable runner that replays synthetic workloads against a target environment and evaluates results against an oracle.
- Deterministic seed: A PRNG seed stored with the oracle to reproduce the same tokenization/beam-selection traces for non-deterministic model outputs.

Design Principles
-----------------
- Determinism where possible: use seeds, fixed model weights (when benchmarking), and deterministic tokenizers for oracle generation.
- Lightweight and hermetic: COSH should run in CI as a job that completes in < 20 minutes for core suites and < 90 minutes for extended suites.
- Observability-first: tests assert telemetry (metrics/traces) in addition to payload correctness.
- Progressive coverage: core, extended, and stress tiers to balance CI time and signal quality.

Specification
-------------
1. Oracle format (JSON)
   - metadata: id (sha256), created_at, author, target_api_version, oracle_version
   - tests: list of test cases; each test case is a flat-record with fields: id, description, endpoint, method, request_payload (string), expected_status (one of: success, client_error, server_error, degraded), allowed_response_schema_hashes (list of hashes), numeric_assertions (list of `{metric_name, min, max}`), telemetry_expectations (list of `{span_name, min_count}`), seed (integer)

   Example (excerpt):
   {
     "id": "core-001",
     "description": "short-chat-completion-stable",
     "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
     "method": "POST",
     "request_payload": "{\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Summarize the policy in one sentence.\"}], \"max_tokens\":60}",
     "expected_status": "success",
     "allowed_response_schema_hashes": ["sha256:..."],
     "numeric_assertions": [{"metric_name":"token_count","min":"10","max":"70"}],
     "telemetry_expectations": [{"span_name":"runtime.infer","min_count":"1"}],
     "seed": "42"
   }

2. Harness modes
   - dry-run: validate oracle JSON syntax and schema only.
   - local: run harness against a developer-local environment with mocking options.
   - ci-core: run core test set in CI for each PR touching API surface or runtime.
   - ci-extended: nightly job against canary and staging clusters to catch low-frequency regressions.

3. Test tiers and budget
   - Core tier: 120–200 test cases, CI runtime target < 20m. Failure blocks PR if related files change.
   - Extended tier: 800–2,000 cases, nightly only. Used for regression detection.
   - Stress tier: 10k+ synthetic events, used in dedicated performance pipelines.

4. Assertions and tolerances
   - Exact match assertions allowed for deterministic fields (status codes, JSON schema hashes, top-k token IDs when seeded).
   - Range assertions for numeric metrics (latency_ms, token_count) with annotated SLAs.
   - Telemetry assertions: require presence of critical spans (runtime.dispatch, runtime.infer, api.auth) and dimension labels (model_variant, shard_id, request_class). Missing critical spans marks the test as failed.

Observability contract
----------------------
- Each test run must emit a test-run trace with tag: test.run_id and test.oracle_id. Traces should link to per-request runtime traces via parent/child relationships.
- Metrics to assert in core suite:
  - cosh.test.success_rate (goal >= 99% for core suite in staging)
  - cosh.runtime.infer.latency.p50/p95/p99 (values depend on test profile; see appendix)
  - cosh.telemetry.span_presence (boolean per required span)

CI integration
--------------
1. PR validation:
   - If a change touches any of: api schema, client SDKs, runtime kernel, routing, or model manifests, run ci-core.
   - ci-core failures for changed areas block merge; failures unrelated to changed files produce non-blocking warnings and create a ticket.

2. Nightly pipeline:
   - Run ci-extended against staging and canary. If core success_rate drops by > 2 percentage points vs. previous successful run, auto-open an incident for investigation.

3. Artifact storage:
   - Oracles are stored in the contract-oracle S3 bucket with key pattern: oracles/{target_api_version}/{oracle_id}.json and signed by the author using repo GPG.

Rollout and Canary guidance
---------------------------
1. Canary policy: when rolling a model or runtime change, run the core harness against the canary cluster before traffic ramp. If any core test fails with expected_status != success or missing telemetry spans, abort rollout and trigger rollback.
2. Progressive enablement: if canary passes, run a 2-hour extended run with sampling at 10% traffic in production (metric-driven ramp). Monitor cosh.test.success_rate and cosh.runtime.infer.latency.p95.

Runbook: failed core suite
-------------------------
1. Triage owner: oncall-runtime (pager duty).
2. Immediate steps:
   a. Retrieve last successful oracle id and recent run artifacts from S3.
   b. Compare failed test IDs and diffs in response schema hashes.
   c. If telemetry spans are missing, check tracer agent versions and environment variable injection in deployment.
   d. If numeric assertions violated (latency/token_count), check recent infra events (GPU preemption, autoscale) and routing logs.
3. Escalation:
   - If > 20% core tests failing or success_rate < 90%, page oncall-sre and oncall-infra; treat as Sev2.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- COSH steward: Priya Ramanathan (eng-infrastructure).
- Owners: eng-serving-runtime (primary), eng-infra (support for CI and artifacts), eng-dx (SDK integrations).
- Review cadence: core suite and oracle format reviewed quarterly; oracle artifact rotation annually.

Appendix A — Example CLI usage
-----------------------------
# validate oracle
redwood-cosh validate --oracle s3://oracles/v1/core-2026-01-20.json

# run core suite against staging
redwood-cosh run --oracle s3://oracles/v1/core-2026-01-20.json --target staging --mode ci-core --output results/core-staging-2026-03-08.json

Appendix B — Core test matrix (excerpt)
--------------------------------------
| test_id | endpoint                 | intent                  | key_assertions                  | latency_budget_ms |
|---------|--------------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------|
| core-001| /v1/chat/completions     | short summarization     | status=success, span=infer      | 250               |
| core-012| /v1/completions          | streaming long-form     | partial_chunk_count>=3, span=stream.write | 1200         |
| core-024| /v1/embeddings           | vector stability        | vector_dim=1536, cosine_stable >0.95 | 100           |

Notes and limitations
---------------------
- COSH does not attempt to prove semantic equivalence for open-ended generation — we use token-level or schema-level checks with human-in-the-loop for extended validation.
- Oracle maintenance is an operational cost: owners must keep gold samples up-to-date when intentional behavioral changes are introduced.
